classification.core: The output is a robot application that meets a customer/site workflow and performance requirement: interfaces, configuration, validation, commissioning and handoff. This guide can explain industrial cells and deployed robotic applications while keeping distinct interface stacks visible.
boundaries: Internal subsystem or product bring-up is adjacent, not the central customer-application output.
Autonomous truck, aircraft, maritime and off-road deployment share integration/debugging practices but are not an industrial robot-cell sample.
Pre-sales scoping is adjacent; distinguish requirements/design/handoff from commissioning ownership.
Post-handover uptime repair centers on field service.
A learning coach and training-content tooling are outside this guide even when the title says AI Application Engineer.

portfolio.name: Simulated workcell integration and acceptance bench
portfolio.level: Technical learner with Python/Linux fundamentals; ROS 2 topic/launch basics before the extension.
portfolio.coreBuild: Implement a Python state machine coordinating simulated conveyor, detector and pick station. Publish a small interface contract for ready/request/busy/done/fault, command IDs, units, timeouts and reset/recovery. Connect it to a localhost PyModbus simulator for I/O; no physical robot or PLC required.
progression: First validate one complete command/acknowledge cycle and reject stale or duplicated command IDs.
Add ROS 2 nodes as a separate extension: orchestrator and simulated robot/station; define topic types and QoS explicitly.
Inject unavailable server, invalid register address, missing completion, delayed signal and node restart. For ROS extension add incompatible QoS and stopped publisher cases.
Measure successful cycles/attempts, cycle-time distribution and recovery time against self-declared acceptance criteria; retain failed runs, logs and a before/after fix.

Deliver interface table, architecture sketch, acceptance matrix, automated test results, reproduction instructions, short demo and handover runbook. For ROS extension record relevant topics with ros2 bag and use launch_testing.
portfolio.safetyScope: All plant behavior is simulated. Fault detection/recovery in application code is a learning exercise, not safety-rated stopping, industrial cell certification or authorization to commission physical equipment.
portfolio.rationale: Exercises interfaces, configuration, cross-component debugging, performance evidence and handoff seen in selected integration postings without requiring an industrial cell.

primaryReferences.supports: ROS 2 QoS covers reliability, durability, deadline, lifespan and liveliness; incompatible requested/offered QoS may prevent messages. Supports testing a deliberately incompatible profile and stale-signal handling in a lab. These mechanisms do not establish industrial functional safety.

launch_testing supports active tests with nodes running and post-shutdown tests, uses unittest, can integrate with colcon test, and the tutorial isolates tests using ROS domain IDs. Supports repeatable acceptance checks of multiple communicating nodes.

ros2 bag records and replays topic data. Supports sharing a reproducible failure recording alongside a test report; project can restrict itself to topic recording rather than relying on service introspection features.

Official index identifies application protocol function-code specification and TCP/IP client/server/gateway implementation guide. Supports reading request/response and register interface documentation; not evidence that Modbus is universal across robot jobs.

Simulator offers JSON server/device configuration, TCP server, discrete/coils/register types, invalid register exception responses and register manipulation via actions, Web UI, REST API or writes. Supports an entirely simulated I/O handshake and injected invalid-address cases.

US OSHA technical guidance discusses application-specific documented risk assessment before commissioning, involvement of user/workers and verification/validation of risk-reduction measures. The chapter references older standard editions; use as responsibility context, not a claim of current worldwide legal requirements or certification authority.
